content:
As part of an effort to generalize MultilinearMapto allow for semilinear maps there is an opportunity to introduce notation analogous to those already in place for (Continuous)LinearMap, ContinuousMultilinearMap and AlternatingMap.
My proposal for multilinear maps (see #43877) is

  • M →ₘₗ[R] N for MultilinearMap R M N, mirroring the notation M →ₗ[R] N for LinearMap R M N.
  • M [×n]→ₗ[R] N for MultilinearMap R (fun _ : Fin n => M) N, mirroring the notation M [×n]→L[R] N for ContinuousMultilinearMap R (fun _ : Fin n => M) N.
  • M [^ι]→ₗ[R] N for MultilinearMap R (fun _ : ι => M) N, mirroring the notation M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[R] N for AlternatingMap R M N ι.

and when generalized to multi-semilinear maps (to be added to #42534) also

  • M →ₘₛₗ[σ] N
  • M [×n]→ₛₗ[σ] N
  • M [^ι]→ₛₗ[σ] N

Do these look okay? Any suggestions to improve these or entirely different notation schemes to consider? Personally I'm not thrilled with the "[^ι]→" for a general non-dependent type...

The second is obviously fine since it mirrors the continuous version.
The first and third are the real ones to discuss
I wonder if we can just have a single notation though (like the first) and then if you want to do the second and third you can just write (fun _ : Fin n => M) →ₘₗ[R] N and (fun _ : ι => M) →ₘₗ[R] N

Monica Omar said:

if you want to do the second and third you can just write (fun _ : Fin n => M) →ₘₗ[R] N and (fun _ : ι => M) →ₘₗ[R] N

I agree with this. A cleaner solution may be to have a good notation for (fun _ : Fin n => M) / (fun _ : ι => M) (for example M^⊕ι) and then use the →ₘₗ[R] notation everywhere instead of having seperate cases for the `(fun _ : Fin n => M) / (fun _ : ι => M) cases.

Eric Wieser said:

Older discussion at #general > Notation for `multilinear_map` @ 💬

I see that for mathlib3 the proposal was →ₗₘ so that the continuous version could be →Lₘ.
Thinking ahead maybe →ₗₘ/→ₛₗₘ is better to adopt than →ₘₗ/→ₘₛₗ since when it comes time for notation for continuous multilinear maps →Lₘ/→SLₘ seems preferable over →ML/→MSL or →ₘL/→ₘSL (at least to me).
